Answer: B
Reason: The serial chest X-rays (Figures 1a, 3a, 4a, 6a) demonstrate a clear progression from initial nodular densities predominantly in the middle and lower lung fields to widespread, diffuse bilateral involvement with extensive infiltrative lesions and areas of radiolucency over time. This pattern of worsening diffuse disease aligns with the natural history of progressive bronchioloalveolar carcinoma (now invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma), ruling out stability, regression, or isolated upper lobe onset.
